title: Nessa and the Lost Bunny
markdown:
Nessa the young witch lived in a little cottage. Its roof was bright blue, like the sky! Smoke puffed out the chimney, smelling yummy like cinnamon and sunshine. Her broomstick leaned by the door, ready for a quick fly. But tonight, Nessa was trying something new. She was practicing a spell to make her teacups dance! She hummed a happy, bubbly tune. Her glasses sat on her nose. She wiggled her fingers. "Dance, little teacups, dance!" she whispered. One teacup wiggled its handle. Then another did a little shimmy! Oh, it was so much fun! The teacups twirled and tapped on the table like they were at a big party.

Suddenly, a tiny, worried squeak came from just outside her door. It was a sound so small, like a tiny whisper! Nessa blinked. "That doesn't sound like a dancing teacup," she whispered. Her bright, curious eyes got wide with worry. She tiptoed over and peeked out. And there, by her doorstep, was a rabbit. This was a very fluffy rabbit. His ears were soft like dandelion fluff. His tail wagged like a little puffball. He looked a little bit lost. He sighed a tiny sigh.

"Oh, you poor thing!" Nessa said softly. Her heart felt warm like melted butter. She scooped him up gently. He felt warm and soft, like a little cloud. "Are you lost, little one?" she asked. Her voice was as gentle as a butterfly's wing. The rabbit just nudged her hand with his little pink nose. He didn't have a collar, or a little sign. "Hmm," Nessa thought. She stroked his soft fur. It felt like velvet. "It's getting late," she said. "The Misty Crags can be tricky when it's getting dark. But I can't leave you here all alone." Nessa knew what she had to do. She would help this little rabbit find his home.

"Don't you worry," she said to the rabbit. He was snuggled in her arms, feeling safe. "We'll find your cozy burrow. What's your name?" The rabbit wriggled his nose happily. He made a soft little "Pip-pip!" sound. "Pipkin!" Nessa giggled. "That's a perfect name for such a sweet little fellow!" And so, with Pipkin tucked safely in her arms, Nessa stepped out into the soft, dusky air. The pine trees rustled their needles, making a sound like quiet secrets. The air smelled like damp earth and pinecones.

They walked along a winding path. The moon peeked out from behind a fluffy cloud. It cast long, gentle shadows that danced like playful sprites. Nessa's heart felt a little flutter of worry. What if they couldn't find Pipkin's home? What if he was very hungry? Just then, they saw a warm, flickering light ahead. It peeked through the trees like a friendly firefly. It was a small cottage, like Nessa's own. Outside, a wizard was looking very hard at a very, very big map. This was Wizard Zigzag. He loved maps! He sometimes got them mixed up, just like his long white beard.

"Excuse me, Wizard Zigzag?" Nessa called out. Her voice was clear and bright. The wizard jumped a little. He almost tripped over his map! It was spread out all over his front lawn. "Oh! Hello there, young Nessa! And who is this little fellow you have there?" he asked. His eyes twinkled like stars. "This is Pipkin," Nessa explained. She held the rabbit a little closer. "He seems to be lost. Do you know any rabbit burrows around here? He looks like he needs to be home for supper." Wizard Zigzag smoothed out his map. It was so big it covered his garden. "Rabbit burrows, you say? Let me see..." He squinted at a spot that looked like a spilled ink blot. "Ah, yes! According to this map of the Great Cloud Migration… no, wait, that's the map of the Singing Streams. Hmm, perhaps it's this one here, the Guide to Edible Mushrooms? Or this one, the Atlas of Ancient Acorns?"

Nessa smiled kindly. Her brow creased just a little with thought. "Maybe we could look at a simpler map, one that shows paths and homes, Wizard Zigzag? Something a little less… twisty?" Wizard Zigzag's bushy eyebrows shot up. "A simpler map? Oh, my dear child, that's a curious thought! I do have one somewhere," he rummaged through a pile of scrolls. "Ah, here we are!" he exclaimed. He pulled out a map that was much smaller and much, much clearer. "This is the Map of Peaceful Paths! It shows all the lovely little homes where everyone is happy and safe." Nessa peered at it. It wasn't as grand or as colorful as the others, but it was much, much clearer. There, near a patch of bright green clover, was a little drawing of a rabbit hole. A tiny, wagging tail was peeking out!

"That's it!" Nessa exclaimed. Her voice was full of excitement. "That looks just like Pipkin's home!" Pipkin wriggled happily in her arms, as if he agreed. Wizard Zigzag beamed. His smile stretched from ear to ear. "Wonderful! You see, my dear, sometimes the simplest maps are the most useful. They don't get all tangled up. And sometimes," he winked, his eyes dancing, "a wagging tail is the best guide of all. It knows the way home better than any parchment." He carefully folded the Map of Peaceful Paths and handed it to Nessa. "Thank you so much, Wizard Zigzag!" Nessa said warmly. She held Pipkin close and followed the clear path on the map.

Soon, they came to a small, welcoming burrow. It glowed softly in the moonlight. It looked cozy and warm. A few other rabbits were peeking out, their noses twitching happily. Pipkin gave a happy "Pip-pip-pip!" He wriggled to be put down. He hopped right towards the burrow. He turned back to give Nessa one last happy wag of his tail before disappearing inside. He was home for supper and a cozy sleep with his family.

Nessa watched him go. Her heart felt as warm as a mug of hot cocoa. She had helped a friend! That felt like the best kind of magic. As she walked back to her cottage, the moonlight sparkled on the grass like tiny diamonds. The whispering pines seemed to sing a gentle lullaby. And Nessa knew, with all her heart, that even a little witch with slightly crooked glasses could make a big difference in the world with just a little kindness and a good, clear map.
characters: Nessa the young witch, a rabbit
